transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah… so, I’m here because I’m spending way too much time rechecking things. It sounds kind of small when I say it like that, but it’s started taking over parts of my day.

Like, I’ll check my dressing supplies, or the door locks, or files I’m working on — dimensions, revision notes, that kind of thing — and I don’t just check once and move on. I feel like I have to go through the same routine again and again until it feels… I don’t know, safe enough, or until the anxiety drops enough that I’m allowed to move on. If I stop too early, it feels like something is unfinished or wrong, and then I can’t really focus on anything else.

I’m an engineer, so some checking is normal in my work, obviously, but this feels different. It’s not just being careful. It’s like I lose hours to it, and even when I know I already checked, I still feel pulled back into doing it again.
When you’re rechecking these things, do you have specific thoughts that come up — like a fear that something bad will happen if you don’t check, or thoughts that are distressing and hard to control?

Yeah. It’s not just a vague “maybe I should check again” feeling. There’s usually a very specific thought that cuts in, even when I know I already did the thing.

Like with the wound area, even after I’ve cleaned it and I can literally remember cleaning it, I’ll get this thought like, “What if you missed one tiny spot?” And then my mind jumps to, “What if that becomes infected because you were careless?” It feels disproportionate when I say it out loud, but in the moment it feels urgent, like I can’t just leave it alone.

And with work, it’s similar but framed around the CAD files. I’ll review a dimension or a revision note, and then almost immediately I’ll think, “What if there’s one small mistake you didn’t catch?” And it doesn’t stop there — it turns into this fear that a design error could lead to someone getting hurt. Even if logically I know I checked it, and even if there’s no real evidence I missed anything, the thought keeps coming back. I try to reason with it, like, “You already reviewed that,” but it doesn’t really settle it. It just keeps pressing until I check again.

Other candidates (F41.0, F40.2) are ruled out due to the specific nature of obsessions and compulsions that go beyond generalized anxiety or phobic disorders.

inference_history.note: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors driven by anxiety and a sense of incompleteness, which suggests obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.2). The presentation also includes prominent anxiety, which could indicate generalized anxiety disorder (F41.0) or a specific anxiety disorder such as obsessive-compulsive disorder. Additionally, the compulsive rechecking could be a manifestation of obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (F40.2), though less likely given the described distress and functional impact.
